beats.text: Your rent has a new suspect. About 7 billion dollars of OpenAI shares reportedly just turned into money staff can spend.
beats.show_cue: The coverage's lead art with the OpenAI logo, then real San Francisco street footage the Operator shoots, a steep street with Victorians.

beats.text: Shares in a private company are paper until somebody organises a sale, and that's what a tender offer is: the company lines up new investors, staff sell them existing shares, and nobody waits for an IPO. OpenAI hasn't confirmed a word of it.
beats.show_cue: The open coverage headline with its August 10 date, then an Operator-built three box diagram, staff shares to new investors to cash. Credit the original financial outlet in a small text card only, it is paywalled.

beats.text: For scale, about 500 billion dollars was reportedly lined up for data centres the same day. Machine money dwarfs people money. People money lands on one city's streets.
beats.show_cue: An Operator-built comparison card, 7 billion beside 500 billion. Credit the papers by name in small text, never screen record them, both are paywalled.

beats.text: The San Francisco rent panic, though, is a headline's leap, not a study. Nobody's measured where this money went, and rents move on rates, supply and construction all at once.
beats.show_cue: The coverage's housing paragraph held long enough to read as one news sentence, not a finding.

beats.text: And a tender puts no new money into OpenAI, so it tells you nothing about the business.
beats.show_cue: Operator on camera, one plain text caption, no graphs.

beats.text: Follow Straw Motion. We skip the hype, you get the story.
beats.show_cue: Straw Motion logo end card, no overlay.
